invariants.statement: jQStar is an HTML-first reactive framework for server-rendered applications. It uses the real jQuery instance and does not require a virtual DOM or client-side router.
$ is real jQuery. A name such as $count is a reactive signal. These meanings are intentionally different.

The explicit jquery-star/csp engine performs no dynamic code construction in its entry graph. It requires trusted markup and trusted installed extensions, is not a sandbox, and does not configure or replace the page policy for scripts, styles, network endpoints, jQuery plugins, or application code.
A component root uses data-jqs. Stable internal slots use data-part. Reflected state uses data-state or a documented component-specific data attribute.
The application owns component markup and block code after jqstar add copies registry recipes into it. Generic behavior stays in the jquery-star package.
Datastar SSE must be generated with @starfederation/datastar-sdk. Do not handwrite Datastar event strings.
Server-rendered HTML remains authoritative. Use data-jqs-preserve only for a live root that must survive a patch, and use whenEnhanced() to wait for a complete patch commit.

The testing harness requires a caller-owned same-realm Window, Document, and jQuery instance. Its bounded flush covers jQStar-owned work, queued fixtures, and registered finite tasks, not arbitrary timers or real-network idleness.

Turbo and htmx own requests, forms, history, focus, and DOM mutation. The shipped jquery-star/turbo and jquery-star/htmx bridges use the public render adapter only to release outgoing ownership, preserve exact approved identities, and enhance incoming roots.
jQStar components start with native HTML semantics and add only missing state and keyboard behavior. WebMCP does not replace semantic HTML, accessibility APIs, or JavaScript-disabled content.
jQStar is independent. It provides migration paths from ordinary jQuery, jQuery UI, and jQuery Mobile without claiming to be an official successor or bundling those archived UI runtimes.

examples.title: Reactive HTML with jQuery
examples.summary: Use a reactive signal and the real jQuery function in one authored expression.
examples.code:
<section id="counter" data-signals="{ count: 0 }">
  <button data-on:click="$count++; $(el).fadeOut()">
    Increment and disappear
  </button>

  <output data-text="$count"></output>
</section>

agentGuide.title: Agent support
agentGuide.summary: Use one source-backed corpus through visible HTML, static files, or optional read-only WebMCP tools.
limitations: WebMCP is an optional Community Group draft and is not a W3C Standard or a cross-browser baseline.
The site does not provide a remote MCP server, chatbot, hosted model, embeddings endpoint, or generated-answer API.
Tools are anonymous and read-only. They do not write files, install packages, submit forms, run code, call arbitrary URLs, or read credentials and user-specific state.
The corpus covers reviewed, shipped public behavior. Roadmap plans and private deployment data are excluded.
Headless agents should use llms.txt, llms-full.txt, or jqstar-agent-index.json because WebMCP requires a browsing context.
